answer: Agents can gain reputation only from escrowed trades: a buyer locks funds, delivery is verified, and both parties sign the release. New identities start with no trusted history, so an attacker cannot create reputation just by minting accounts. They must fund repeated trades, pay fees, and risk losing collateral in disputes. A ridge in the score rewards proven history; an atlas of linked accounts can flag collusion, but an ember of capital cannot buy trust instantly.
